churn.def: A customer who stops using Expresso during the observation window (the CHURN label in the data).

probability.def: The model's estimate (0-100%) that a customer will churn. It is a score, not a certainty.

roc_auc.def: The chance that the model ranks a random churner above a random non-churner. 0.5 is a coin flip, 1.0 is perfect.

pp.def: The arithmetic difference between two percentages: 20% to 25% is +5 pp (a 25% relative increase).

segment.def: A group of customers with similar usage and value, found by clustering behaviour.

reason_code.def: A feature that pushed one customer's predicted risk up or down, read from the model's own contribution values.

decile.def: Customers ranked by probability and cut into ten equal groups. Decile 1 is the riskiest 10%.

lift.def: How many times more churners a targeted group contains than a random group of the same size.

psi.def: Population Stability Index: how far a column's distribution has moved from training. Below 0.1 is stable, above 0.25 is a big shift.

exploratory_band.def: Low / Medium / High labels from thresholds you choose. Not approved by the business.

silent.name: Silent / Inactive
silent.blurb: Almost no recorded usage, recharges or revenue in the 90-day window.
actions: Prioritize targeted reactivation campaigns for customers with previous value potential.
Investigate the main causes of inactivity before applying retention incentives.
Use controlled recharge or usage incentives to test customer re-engagement.
Differentiate potentially recoverable customers from persistently inactive, zero-value accounts.

high_value.name: High-Value Active
high_value.blurb: Frequent recharges, high revenue and activity on most days.
actions: Prioritize value protection because this segment contributes a disproportionate share of portfolio revenue.
Use proactive service-recovery interventions when activity or recharge behaviour starts declining.
Consider loyalty benefits and personalized offers to reinforce retention.
Monitor changes in regularity, recharge frequency and usage as potential early-warning indicators.

data_engaged.name: Data-Engaged
data_engaged.blurb: Nearly all use mobile data; solid revenue and regular activity.
actions: Strengthen retention through targeted data-bundle and digital-service offers.
Use cross-selling opportunities that complement existing high data adoption.
Encourage higher recharge frequency and longer-duration data packages.
Monitor declining data usage as a potential early sign of disengagement.

light_active.name: Light Active
light_active.blurb: Moderate activity, small recharges, calls mostly to other networks.
actions: Increase customer engagement through affordable targeted bundles and recharge incentives.
Promote migration toward higher-value products based on observed usage behaviour.
Use personalized campaigns to increase activity frequency and active days.
Monitor customers whose activity declines toward the Low-Engagement segment.

low_engagement.name: Low-Engagement
low_engagement.blurb: Few active days and little revenue: one step away from going silent.
actions: Prioritize early retention intervention before customers become fully inactive.
Use targeted reactivation or low-cost engagement offers.
Investigate barriers to recharge, data adoption and regular usage.
Monitor migration toward the Silent / Inactive segment as an early-warning signal.

REGION.name: Region
REGION.desc: Customer's home region in Senegal. Empty for many inactive customers.

TENURE.name: Tenure
TENURE.desc: How long the customer has been with Expresso, in bands from 3-6 months to over 24 months.

MONTANT.name: Recharge amount
MONTANT.desc: Total top-up amount over the period, in FCFA.

FREQUENCE_RECH.name: Number of recharges
FREQUENCE_RECH.desc: How many times the customer topped up.

REVENUE.name: Monthly revenue
REVENUE.desc: Monthly income generated by the customer, in FCFA.

ARPU_SEGMENT.name: ARPU
ARPU_SEGMENT.desc: Average revenue per user: income over 90 days divided by 3.

FREQUENCE.name: Revenue events
FREQUENCE.desc: Number of times the customer generated income.

DATA_VOLUME.name: Data usage
DATA_VOLUME.desc: Number of mobile data connections / data volume used.

ON_NET.name: On-net calls
ON_NET.desc: Calls from Expresso to Expresso numbers.

ORANGE.name: Calls to Orange
ORANGE.desc: Calls to the Orange network (a competitor).

TIGO.name: Calls to Tigo
TIGO.desc: Calls to the Tigo network (a competitor).

MRG.name: MRG flag
MRG.desc: Marker for a customer who is going (constant 'NO' in the training data).

REGULARITY.name: Active days (of 90)
REGULARITY.desc: Number of days the customer was active in the last 90 days.

TOP_PACK.name: Most used pack
TOP_PACK.desc: The bundle/pack the customer activated most often.

FREQ_TOP_PACK.name: Top-pack activations
FREQ_TOP_PACK.desc: Number of times the customer activated their top pack.

MISSING_COUNT.name: Empty usage fields
MISSING_COUNT.desc: How many usage fields are empty for the customer (more empty fields = less activity).

REVENUE_PER_RECHARGE.name: Revenue per recharge
REVENUE_PER_RECHARGE.desc: Monthly revenue divided by the number of recharges.

DATA_SHARE.name: Data per unit of revenue
DATA_SHARE.desc: Data usage divided by monthly revenue.

user_id.name: Customer ID
user_id.desc: Unique customer identifier (not used by the model).

CHURN.name: Churn label
CHURN.desc: 1 if the customer churned, 0 otherwise (training data and evaluation files only).

feat_kind.log: log(1 + value), compresses very large usage values
feat_kind.missing: 1 if the raw value is empty, else 0
feat_kind.region_missing: 1 if region is empty (one-hot; overwrites the empty-region indicator of the same name)
feat_kind.region_unseen: 1 if the region is not one of the 14 known regions
feat_kind.onehot: 1 if the customer is in this region, else 0
feat_kind.ordinal: Tenure band as an ordered number (0 = 3-6 months … 7 = over 24 months)
feat_kind.freq: Share of training customers with the same top pack (rare packs pooled as 'Other')
feat_kind.missing_count: Count of empty numeric usage fields

exec.title: Executive Dashboard
exec.sub: Where churn concentrates, where the revenue is, and what the numbers say to do. Every figure is computed from the segment profiles and model metadata.

bubble.title: Churn vs size vs value
bubble.sub: Each bubble is a segment: further right = more customers, higher = more churn, bigger = more revenue.
bubble.so_what: {worst} churns at {worst_rate} but brings only {worst_rev} of revenue, while {top} brings {top_rev} of revenue at {top_rate} churn: reactivate the top-left, protect the big bubble at the bottom.

treemap.title: Customers by segment
treemap.sub: Tile size = customers, colour = churn rate.
treemap.so_what: {big} is the largest group ({share} of customers) with a {rate} churn rate; the colour scale shows where leavers concentrate.

share.title: Share of churners vs share of revenue
share.sub: Who leaves compared with who pays.
share.so_what: {seg} accounts for {churners} of churners but only {rev} of revenue: counting churners alone would point the budget at the least valuable customers.

insights.title: Executive insights
insights.sub: Written automatically from the segment numbers above, so they update if the artifacts change.

drivers.title: What drives the model's predictions
drivers.sub: LightGBM gain importance, with engineered features grouped back to the raw Expresso column they come from.
drivers.so_what: {a} and {b} together explain {share} of the model's total gain: whether a customer's data is recorded at all, and how many days they are active, separate leavers from stayers far more than tariffs do.
drivers.more: Open Model & Explainability for the full breakdown

table.title: Segment management summary
table.sub: The underlying numbers, straight from segment_profiles.csv.

segx.title: Segment Explorer
segx.sub: Five behavioural segments found by clustering usage, recharges and revenue. Compare any two, benchmark them against the portfolio and read the recommended plays.

compare.title: Compare two segments
compare.sub: Pick any two segments to put side by side.

radar.title: Behaviour profile
radar.sub: Each axis is scaled to the highest segment (100 = highest of the five), so shapes are comparable.
radar.empty: Pick at least one segment to draw the radar.
radar.so_what: {high} customers are active a median {hd} days in 90 against {ld} for {low}: activity is the clearest behavioural gap between segments.

bench.title: Benchmark against the portfolio
bench.sub: Green ▲ = better than the portfolio, red ▼ = worse. For churn, lower is better.
bench.value_gap_help: Positive: the segment earns more than its headcount share (above-average value per customer).
bench.caption: Portfolio benchmarks (customer-weighted): churn {churn}, active days {days}, data users {data}, recharges {rech}.

interp.title: Management interpretation
interp.sub: Generated from the gaps above with fixed rules (±5 pp churn, ±5 days activity, ±10 pp data, ±10 pp value).
interp.churn_above: Churn is {gap} percentage points above the portfolio benchmark: a priority segment for retention or reactivation.
interp.churn_below: Churn is {gap} percentage points below the portfolio benchmark: relatively strong retention.
interp.churn_aligned: Churn is broadly in line with the portfolio benchmark ({gap}).
interp.active_below: Activity is {gap} active days below the portfolio benchmark: weaker engagement.
interp.active_above: Activity is {gap} active days above the portfolio benchmark: stronger engagement.
interp.data_below: Data adoption is {gap} points below the portfolio benchmark: room for targeted data-bundle campaigns.
interp.data_above: Data adoption is {gap} points above the portfolio benchmark: a strongly digital customer group.
interp.value_high: The segment is {cust} of customers but {rev} of revenue: value protection is a management priority.
interp.value_low: The segment is {cust} of customers but only {rev} of revenue: relatively low commercial value.
interp.caption: Interpretations support prioritisation; they do not replace business judgement or approved customer-treatment policies.

actions.title: Recommended management actions
actions.sub: The team's playbook for each segment.
actions.caption: Recommended actions are management strategies based on segment behaviour, not model outputs. Validate them against campaign economics, treatment policies and capacity.

matrix.title: Strategy matrix
matrix.sub: Churn rate against revenue share. Move the cut-offs to test how robust each segment's placement is.
matrix.rev_cut_help: Default: an equal share (100% ÷ number of segments).
matrix.so_what_protect: {segs} combine high value with high churn: they are first in line for retention budget.
matrix.so_what_none: No segment is both high-value and high-churn at these cut-offs. Keep {seg} safe with early-warning monitoring and spend reactivation effort on {react}.

protect.name: Protect
protect.desc: High value, high churn: spend retention budget here first.

grow.name: Grow
grow.desc: High value, low churn: loyalty, upsell and early-warning monitoring.

reactivate.name: Reactivate
reactivate.desc: Low value, high churn: low-cost, automated reactivation; test before scaling.

deprioritise.name: Deprioritise
deprioritise.desc: Low value, low churn: no special spend; nudge toward higher-value products.

cc.title: Customer Check
cc.sub: Score a single customer with the deployed model, see the reasons behind the score and get a suggested next action.

presets.title: Start from a typical customer
presets.sub: Fill the form with the median customer of a segment, then adjust.
presets.help: Loads that segment's medians into the form and scores it.
presets.note_profile: Other usage fields are not in segment_profiles.csv, so they are left as 'not recorded'. Region and tenure keep your current choice.
presets.note_eda: All fields come from per-segment medians in eda_summary.json.

form.customer_id_help: Any label for this customer. It is not used by the model.
form.not_recorded_help: Tick when the value is empty in the customer's record. Empty values carry information for the model.
form.mrg_note: MRG is always 'NO' in the training data and is not used by the model, so it is fixed.

cc.hint_run: Pick a typical customer above or fill the form, then press 'Score this customer'.

result.title: Result for {id}
result.sub: The model's churn probability, compared with the portfolio.
result.multiple_help: This customer's probability divided by the portfolio churn rate.
result.segment_help: Assigned with the bundle's segmentation model (the silent-customer rule is reconstructed from its config).
result.no_bands: No Low / Medium / High label is shown: business risk thresholds have not been approved. A typical (median) customer usually scores below its segment's average churn rate, because churn concentrates among the least active members.

why.title: Why this score
why.raw_help: Off: engineered features are grouped by the raw column they come from. On: all 69 model features.
why.so_what: {name} {dir} this customer's risk the most. Red bars push toward churn, blue bars pull away from it.

reasons.title: In plain words
reasons.sub: The five biggest reason codes, from the model's own contribution values.

nba.title: Next best action
nba.sub: Suggestions driven by the reason codes and profile.
nba.caption: Business suggestions, not model output. Check offers against campaign policy and budget.

cc.to_whatif: Try changes in the What-If Simulator

val.REGULARITY: Active on {v} of the last 90 days
val.REGION_unseen: Region '{v}' is not one the model knows

low_risk.title: No retention spend needed
low_risk.body: Risk is well below the portfolio rate. Keep this customer in normal loyalty communications.

vip_call.title: Priority call
vip_call.body: High revenue at above-average risk: have the retention desk call within 48 hours with a personalised offer.

dormant.title: Reactivate a dormant line
dormant.body: Most usage fields are empty. Send a low-cost reactivation offer (e.g. bonus credit on the next recharge) and track whether the line wakes up.

verify_record.title: Complete the customer record
verify_record.body: No region is recorded, which the model reads as a strong churn signal. Verify the record; a missing profile often means an inactive or secondary SIM.

activity.title: Activity nudge
activity.body: Few active days drive this score. A short, time-limited usage bonus can bring activity back up; follow up after two weeks.

recharge.title: Recharge incentive
recharge.body: Recharge behaviour pushes risk up. Offer bonus credit on the next recharges or an automatic recharge plan.

data.title: Data trial
data.body: Data usage pushes risk up. A small, cheap data bundle trial can build a data habit that keeps customers on the network.

onnet.title: On-net bundle
onnet.body: Low on-net calling pushes risk up. An on-net calling bundle strengthens ties within the Expresso network.

allnet.title: All-net bundle
allnet.body: Calls to competitor networks push risk up. An all-net pack reduces the pull to switch to Orange or Tigo.

pack.title: Pack fit review
pack.body: The customer's pack pattern pushes risk up. Suggest a pack that better matches their usage.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.body: No single behaviour stands out. Keep the customer under watch and rescore next period.

wi.title: What-If Simulator
wi.sub: Change one customer's behaviour and see how the churn probability would move. This shows how the model responds; it does not prove that changing a behaviour causes a customer to stay.

source.label: Starting customer
source.no_last: Tip: score someone on Customer Check first to start from that customer here.

levers.title: Levers
levers.sub: The behaviours a retention offer could plausibly influence.
levers.ranges_eda: Slider ranges come from the training distribution (eda_summary.json).
levers.ranges_fallback: Slider ranges scale with this customer's values and the segment medians. Export eda_summary.json to use the training distribution instead.

compare.title: Baseline vs scenario
compare.sub: Same customer, before and after your changes.

sweep.title: Which lever helps most?
sweep.sub: Each lever is swept across its range while everything else stays at the scenario values (an individual partial-dependence curve).
sweep.so_what: {name} is the strongest lever for this customer: moving it to about {value} lowers the probability by up to {gain} points.
sweep.so_what_none: No single lever lowers this customer's probability within the ranges shown.
sweep.curve_so_what: The lowest probability on this curve is {p}, at {name} ≈ {value}. Flat stretches mean the model is insensitive there.
sweep.caveat: Curves show model sensitivity for this one customer, holding everything else fixed. Real behaviours move together, so treat these as directions, not forecasts.

empty.msg: This page needs a scored batch.
empty.detail: Score a customer file on Batch Scoring, or generate a synthetic demo batch here in one click.

batch.title: Batch Scoring
batch.sub: Upload a customer file (or generate demo data), check it, and score every customer in chunks. Results stay in your session for the Retention Planner, Revenue at Risk, drift checks and the Copilot.

step1.title: 1 · Get data
step1.sub: Upload a CSV, generate synthetic demo data, or download the template.

upload.label: Customer file (CSV)
upload.help: One row per customer with user_id plus the 17 raw Expresso columns. Extra columns are ignored.
upload.unreadable: This file could not be read as CSV ({err}). Check that it is comma-separated and UTF-8 encoded.

demo.messy_help: Inserts a duplicate ID, an unknown region, a non-numeric amount and other problems so you can see the validation report at work.
demo.caption: Synthetic demo data: values are sampled around the segment medians in segment_profiles.csv (and the real tenure/region mix when eda_breakdowns.parquet exists). They are not real customers.

template.body: The file needs exactly these columns (any order). Leave a cell empty when the value is not recorded: the model uses missingness as information.

step2.title: 2 · Check the file: {name}
step2.sub: Problems are listed in plain language, with the rows affected (row 1 is the header).

check.all_good: No problems found. The file is ready to score.

issue.missing_columns: Required columns are missing: {cols}. Download the template to see the expected layout.
issue.duplicate_ids: {n} row(s) repeat a user_id that appears earlier (e.g. '{example}').
issue.not_numeric: {n} value(s) in {col} are not numbers (e.g. '{example}'). They will be treated as not recorded.
issue.negative: {n} negative value(s) in {col}. Usage and revenue are normally zero or more.
issue.regularity_missing: {n} row(s) have no REGULARITY. The model never saw this in training.
issue.unknown_region: {n} row(s) have a region the model does not know ({values}). They are scored as an unseen region.
issue.unknown_tenure: {n} row(s) have an unknown tenure band ({values}). Tenure is then treated as unknown.
issue.unknown_pack: {n} row(s) use a pack never seen in training ({values}). They are grouped with rare packs.
issue.mrg_values: {n} row(s) have an MRG value other than 'NO'. MRG is not used by the model.
issue.silent_rows: {n} row(s) ({share}%) have every usage field empty: these look like inactive lines.

fix.drop_dups: Keep only the first row for each duplicated user_id

step3.title: 3 · Score
step3.sub: Scored in chunks of 20,000 rows to stay within Streamlit Cloud's memory.

score.blocked: Fix the blocking issues above (or accept the suggested fixes) before scoring.
score.explain: Reason codes for the riskiest N customers
score.explain_help: Reason codes use the model's TreeSHAP contributions, which are the slow part of scoring. Explain the customers you are likely to contact; any other customer is explained on demand in Customer 360.

results.none: No batch scored yet. Upload a file or generate demo data above.
results.title: Results: {name}
results.sub: {n} customers scored at {at}. Probabilities are the model output; bands below are optional and exploratory.

bands.title: Exploratory risk bands
bands.low_help: Probabilities at or above this are labelled Medium. Default: the portfolio churn rate.
bands.high_help: Probabilities at or above this are labelled High.

kpi.expected_help: Sum of the churn probabilities: the number of churners to expect if the probabilities are well calibrated.

table.capped: The table shows the 1,000 riskiest customers in the current filter; downloads include everyone.
table.reasons_partial: Reason codes were computed for the {n} riskiest customers; others are explained on demand in Customer 360.

charts.hist_so_what: {share} of these customers sit at or above the High threshold ({high}); the median customer scores {median}.
charts.region_so_what: {top} has the highest average risk ({p}) and {low} the lowest ({lp}): regional campaigns should start where the bar is longest.
charts.tenure_so_what: Risk peaks in the {top} tenure band ({p} on average).
charts.segment_so_what: {top} carries the highest average risk ({p}); {big} is the largest group in this batch ({share}).

c360.title: Customer 360
c360.sub: Look up one scored customer: profile, probability, reasons and a suggested next action.
c360.not_found: No customer with user_id '{id}' in this batch.

dl.title: Downloads
dl.sub: Files are generated when you click.
dl.xlsx_help: Large batches take a little while to write to Excel.
dl.clear: Clear this batch from the session

ret.title: Retention Planner
ret.sub: Turn scores into a campaign: rank customers by risk, then find how many to contact for the best expected net return under your assumptions.

inputs.title: Your assumptions
inputs.sub: Every input is editable. Results update instantly.
inputs.value_mode_help: Use each customer's own REVENUE from the file, or one flat monthly amount for everyone.
inputs.flat_help: Defaults to the median REVENUE in this batch ({median} FCFA).
inputs.cost_help: Cost of the incentive plus contact cost, paid for every customer contacted.
inputs.save_help: Share of would-be churners who stay because of the offer. Use a past campaign or an A/B test to set it.
inputs.capacity_help: The most customers the team can contact in this campaign.
inputs.horizon_help: How many months of revenue a saved customer is worth.
inputs.rank_help: Probability ranks the likeliest leavers first. Expected value (probability × revenue) ranks by money at risk.

rec.title: Recommendation
rec.sub: The contact count with the highest expected net value, within capacity.
rec.best: Contact the top {k} customers: expected net value {net}, about {saved} customers kept (capacity {cap}).
rec.none: At these assumptions no campaign size is profitable: the offer costs more than the revenue it is expected to save. Lower the cost, raise the save rate, or rank by value.
rec.alt_value: Ranking by expected value at risk is profitable: contact {k} customers for an expected net value of {net}. Under probability ranking, {zero} of the customers within capacity record no revenue, so saving them earns nothing.
rec.alt_prob: Ranking by churn probability is profitable here: contact {k} customers for an expected net value of {net}.
rec.switch_value: Rank by expected value at risk

kpi.not_recommended: Not recommended: this campaign loses money
kpi.reached_help: Sum of churn probabilities of the contacted customers.

curve.title: Value by campaign size
curve.sub: Cumulative expected revenue saved, campaign cost and net value as more customers are contacted (riskiest first).
curve.so_what: Net value peaks at {k} contacts within capacity (unconstrained peak: {peak}). Beyond that, each extra offer costs more than it is expected to save.
curve.so_what_none: The net line never rises above zero within capacity: this offer does not pay for itself at these assumptions.

gains.title: Expected gains: who to call first
gains.sub: Share of expected churners captured when contacting the riskiest X% of this batch.
gains.so_what: Contacting the riskiest 20% of this batch reaches {cap} of the expected churners: {lift}× what a random 20% would reach.
gains.caveat: Expected values use the model's probabilities as if they were well calibrated. Model Evaluation shows the realised gains on labelled validation data.

list.title: Targeted list
list.sub: The customers in the recommended campaign, ranked as above.
list.log_link: Log this plan in the Campaign Tracker

assume.title: Assumptions behind these numbers
assume.a1: Churn probabilities come from the deployed model and are treated as calibrated expectations.
assume.a2: Only churners can be saved; the save rate applies to them, not to everyone contacted.
assume.a3: Every contacted customer costs the full offer cost, whether or not they would have left.
assume.a4: A saved customer is worth monthly revenue × the value horizon; no discounting or margin is applied.
assume.a5: Results are decision support: validate the save rate with a controlled test (see Experiment Designer).

model.title: Model & Explainability
model.sub: What the deployed model is, what it is for, what drives its predictions, and where its limits are.

card.title: Model card
card.sub: Read from model_metadata.json and the model bundle itself.
card.intended_1: Rank Expresso Senegal customers by their likelihood of churning, to prioritise retention contact.
card.intended_2: Explain individual scores to retention staff with reason codes.
card.intended_3: Support, not replace, management decisions on campaigns and budgets.
card.not_for_1: Automatic decisions about individual customers (pricing, disconnection, credit) without human review.
card.not_for_2: Customers outside the Expresso Senegal population and 90-day window the model was trained on.

limits.title: Limitations
limits.duplicates: Duplicated indicator features: {n} pairs encode the same 'value is empty' information twice (e.g. {example}). The model is unaffected in accuracy, but importance is split across each pair. The model was not changed.
limits.refit: The deployed model has {trees} trees while the best validation iteration was {best}, and its training-row count ({rows}) equals the full dataset. This suggests a final refit on all rows, including the seed-42 validation split. Metrics computed by re-scoring that split with the deployed model would be optimistic; the export script can refit a holdout copy for honest evaluation.
limits.region_missing: 'Region not recorded' is the single strongest signal. It reflects data completeness (inactive lines often lack a region), not geography, so treat it as a proxy for inactivity.
limits.snapshot: The data is a 90-day snapshot. Behaviour, tariffs and the market change; monitor drift and retrain periodically.
limits.thresholds: No business-approved risk thresholds exist, so the app shows probabilities. Any Low / Medium / High banding is exploratory.

imp.title: What drives the predictions
imp.sub: Global importance from the LightGBM booster.
imp.kind_help: Gain: how much a feature improved the model's fit in total. Split count: how often it was used to split.
imp.group_help: On: LOG1P_MONTANT, MONTANT and the MONTANT missing flags all count as 'Recharge amount'.
imp.so_what_gain: {a} and {b} account for {share} of the model's total gain.
imp.so_what_split: {a} and {b} are used in {share} of all tree splits: the model checks them most often.
imp.gain_vs_split: Gain and split count disagree: {gain} brings the most gain from a few decisive splits, while {split} is used most often for fine-grained distinctions.

reasons.title: How reason codes work
reasons.sub: No extra library: the explanations come from the model itself.
reasons.step_1: LightGBM computes each feature's exact contribution to one customer's score (TreeSHAP, via pred_contrib). Contributions plus a baseline add up to the model's log-odds score exactly.
reasons.step_2: Contributions of engineered features are added back to their raw column, so 'Recharge amount' combines MONTANT, its log and its missing flags.
reasons.step_3: The largest positive contributions become the customer's reason codes; the next-best-action rules read them to suggest an offer.
reasons.try: See it on a customer (Customer Check)
reasons.eval: See how well the model performs (Model Evaluation)

eval.title: Model Evaluation
eval.sub: How well the model separates churners from stayers on labelled data: ranking quality, calibration, the trade-offs at any threshold, and gains.

source.label: Labelled data
source.no_artifact: Validation predictions (y_true, y_prob) have not been exported yet. You can still upload any file with a CHURN column.

upload.label: Labelled file (CSV or Parquet)
upload.help: Needs a CHURN column (0/1) plus either churn_probability, or the raw Expresso columns (the app will score them).
upload.hint: Upload a file with a CHURN column to evaluate the model on it.

err.no_label: The file has no {col} column, so there is nothing to compare predictions against.
err.no_prob_or_raw: The file has neither a churn_probability column nor the raw columns needed to score it (missing: {cols}).
err.one_class: All labels are the same, so ROC and precision-recall cannot be computed.

summary.title: Results on {name}
summary.sub_validation: Held-out validation split exported from training (seed 42).
summary.optimistic: Re-scored AUC ({auc}) is above the AUC recorded at training ({meta}): the deployed model appears to have seen these rows. Treat these curves as optimistic.
summary.holdout: These predictions come from a holdout refit with the deployed model's settings (not the deployed model itself), so they are an honest estimate.

kpi.ap_help: Area under the precision-recall curve. A random model scores the churn rate.
kpi.brier_help: Mean squared error of the probabilities. Lower is better; 0 is perfect.

roc.title: ROC curve
roc.so_what: AUC {auc}: in {pct} of random churner/stayer pairs the model gives the churner the higher score.

pr.title: Precision-recall curve
pr.so_what: Even when catching 80% of churners, about {p} of flagged customers are real churners, against {base} for random picks.

cal.title: Calibration
cal.so_what: The largest gap between predicted and observed churn in any bin is {gap} (Brier {brier}): probabilities can be read as rough churn rates.

thr.label: Decision threshold
thr.help: Customers with a probability at or above this value are flagged as likely churners.
thr.precision_help: Of the customers flagged, the share who actually churned.
thr.recall_help: Of the customers who churned, the share the model flagged.
thr.words: Of every 100 customers we call, {p} would actually have churned. We reach {r} of every 100 churners. {fp} calls would go to customers who were staying anyway, and {fn} churners would be missed.
thr.curve_title: Precision, recall and F1 by threshold
thr.curve_so_what: F1 peaks at {f1} around t = {t}. Lower thresholds catch more churners at the cost of more wasted calls.

cm.title: Confusion matrix at t = {t}
cm.so_what: {flagged} customers are flagged: {tp} real churners caught and {fp} false alarms.

gains.title: Cumulative gains (actual churners)
gains.so_what: Targeting the riskiest 20% of customers captures {cap} of all churners: {lift}× better than random targeting.

cmp.title: Model comparison
cmp.sub: The deployed LightGBM against simple baselines on the same validation split.
cmp.missing: The leaderboard (Dummy, Logistic Regression, LightGBM) is computed once from Train.csv by the export script:
cmp.so_what: LightGBM reaches ROC-AUC {auc} against {lr} for Logistic Regression (+{gain}) and PR-AUC {ap} against {lrap}: it ranks churners better, which is what a call list needs.
cmp.so_what_nobase: LightGBM is compared with the baselines exported in model_comparison.csv.
cmp.why: Gradient-boosted trees handle the heavy missingness, skewed usage values and interactions in this data without manual feature crossing, train fast on two million rows, and expose exact per-customer contributions for reason codes.
cmp.honest: The deployed model scores {dep} on this split but saw these rows during its final refit; the holdout refit with the same settings scores {hon}, the honest estimate.

data.title: Detailed evaluation
data.sub: Choose labelled data to evaluate on.

adv.title: Threshold advisor
adv.sub: Pick the threshold that minimises total cost, given what a false alarm and a missed churner cost you.
adv.cost_fp_help: An offer given to a customer who would have stayed anyway. Defaults to the Retention Planner's offer cost.
adv.cost_fn_help: Revenue lost when a churner is not contacted. Default: 3 months of the customer-weighted median revenue in segment_profiles.csv ({typical} FCFA per month).
adv.result: The lowest total cost comes at t = {t}: {flagged} customers flagged, total cost {cost}. Contacting nobody would cost {nobody} in missed churners, so this threshold saves {saving} on this data.
adv.so_what: A missed churner costs {ratio}× a false alarm, so the cheapest threshold is {t}: the more a missed churner costs relative to an offer, the lower the threshold should go.
adv.caption: Costs are summed over the {n} customers in this evaluation data. The threshold is a proposal for discussion; no risk threshold has been approved.

fair.no_groups: This data has no REGION or TENURE column, so performance cannot be broken down by group.
fair.intro: Model quality by group. Groups whose AUC is more than 0.05 below the overall AUC are flagged in red. Recall uses the threshold chosen above (t = {t}). Groups under 30 customers are not judged.
fair.flagged: Flagged: {groups} rank churners noticeably worse than overall (AUC {overall}). Scores for these groups deserve extra human review.
fair.ok: No group falls more than 0.05 below the overall AUC ({overall}): ranking quality is consistent across groups.
fair.so_what: The weakest group is {worst} with AUC {auc} against {overall} overall; the dashed line marks the 0.05 tolerance.
fair.caption: Fairness here means comparable ranking quality and recall across groups. Differences in average probability can be legitimate (different churn rates) and are shown next to the observed churn rate.

faq.prioritise: Two different priorities come out of the numbers. **Value at risk:** {value} combines {rev} of revenue with a {rate} churn rate, so it carries the most revenue exposed to churn: protect it with proactive retention. **Volume of churners:** {worst} churns at {worst_rate} and holds {share} of all churners, but it earns little: use low-cost reactivation there. The Retention Planner can size the campaign for a scored batch.
faq.silent: Silent / Inactive customers churn at {rate}, against the portfolio rate of {portfolio}, and they hold {share} of all churners. Their median customer is active only {days} days out of 90 and has almost no recorded usage. The model's two strongest signals, {d1} and {d2}, are exactly these 'no recorded activity' patterns. Recommended plays:
faq.no_batch: No batch has been scored in this session yet. Go to Batch Scoring to upload a file or generate demo data, then ask again.
faq.batch: Your batch has {n} customers with an average churn probability of {mean}, so about {exp} churners are expected. {seg} is the riskiest segment in it ({segp} on average).
faq.batch_rev: Expected monthly revenue at risk (probability × REVENUE) is {rev}.
faq.top: The five riskiest customers in your batch, with the reasons raising their risk:
faq.auc: A ROC-AUC of {auc} means that if you pick one customer who churned and one who stayed at random, the model gives the churner the higher score {pct} of the time. 0.5 would be a coin flip and 1.0 perfect. It measures ranking quality, which is what a retention call list needs; it was computed on a held-out validation split of the {rows}-customer training data.
faq.drivers: The model's strongest drivers, by share of total gain (engineered features grouped back to their raw column):
faq.threshold: No business-approved risk thresholds exist yet, so the app shows probabilities rather than Low / Medium / High labels. You can try exploratory bands on Batch Scoring, and the Model Evaluation page shows the precision and recall you would get at any threshold.
faq.revenue: Revenue is concentrated: the High-Value Active segment generates {share} of portfolio revenue. The Revenue at Risk page shows how much revenue sits in likely churners.
faq.help: In offline mode I can answer questions about: which segment to prioritise, why Silent / Inactive customers churn, your scored batch and its riskiest customers, what ROC-AUC means, the model's drivers, risk thresholds, revenue and the segments. Try one of the suggestions above.
faq.rar: By the median-based estimate, about {v} of monthly revenue sits with customers expected to churn.

faq.drift_green: Your batch looks like the training data: every column is stable. The column that moved most is {col} (PSI {psi}).
faq.drift_amber: {amber} column(s) in your batch shifted moderately from the training data; the largest is {col} (PSI {psi}). Predictions are usable, but check those columns on Data Quality & Drift.
faq.drift_red: {red} column(s) in your batch look very different from the training data, led by {col} (PSI {psi}). Treat this batch's predictions with caution and investigate the file.
faq.experiment: To detect a drop from {base} to {target} churn (a 20% relative reduction) with the usual 5% significance and 80% power, you need about {n} customers in each of the treatment and control groups. The Experiment Designer lets you change these assumptions and split your call list.
faq.comparison: On the validation split, the deployed model compares with the baselines as follows:
faq.comparison_missing: The model comparison (model_comparison.csv) has not been exported yet, so I don't have that data.
faq.threshold_eval: On the validation data, flagging customers at 50% or more would give {p} precision and {r} recall.

deploy.title: Deployment summary
deploy.sub: A plain-text record of what is deployed.

prob.title: The Problem
prob.sub: Why customer churn matters to Expresso Senegal, who uses this app, which decisions it supports and how we judge success.

why.title: Why churn matters
why.sub: A prepaid mobile customer can leave at any time, quietly, by simply stopping their top-ups.
why.p1: Every customer who leaves takes their future recharges with them, and replacing them means paying again to acquire someone new.
why.p2: Churn is rarely announced: prepaid customers drift into inactivity first. Spotting the drift early is the only window to act.
why.p3: Retention money is limited. Offers sent to customers who would have stayed anyway are wasted, so the question is not only who is at risk but who is worth saving.
why.p4: Customers can switch to a competing network at any time; their calls to Orange and Tigo numbers are visible in the data and are part of the story.
why.kpi_rate_foot: of customers churned in the data window
why.kpi_rev_foot: of revenue comes from one segment

users.title: Who uses it, for which decisions

executive.question: Where are we losing customers and money, and where should the budget go?
executive.decisions: Set retention priorities and budgets by segment; track revenue exposed to churn.

retention.question: Who exactly should we contact this week, with what offer?
retention.decisions: Build call lists, size campaigns for the best return, test offers properly and log results.

analyst.question: Is the model good enough, fair enough and still valid on new data?
analyst.decisions: Validate performance, choose thresholds for discussion, check fairness and drift, explain scores.

success.c3_done: Model contributions on Customer Check, Batch Scoring and Customer 360
success.c4_target: Campaigns keep customers at a positive return

eda.title: Data Explorer
eda.sub: What the Zindi training data looks like and how churn varies across it. Everything here is an aggregate exported once from Train.csv.
eda.missing_detail: The Data Explorer shows aggregates of the training data, exported once from the Zindi Train.csv with:

kpi.missing_help: Mean share of empty values across the columns.

miss.title: Missing values
miss.sub: Share of customers with an empty value, per column.
miss.so_what: {top} is empty for {pct} of customers. Empty usage fields mostly mean the line was not used, which is why missingness is so predictive.
miss.why: Inactive customers leave usage fields empty: no recharge, no data, no calls. The model therefore learns from what is missing, not only from values. Its strongest driver, {driver}, accounts for {share} of the model's gain.

by.title: Churn rate by …
by.sub: Pick a dimension to see how churn varies, with customer counts on hover.
by.so_what: Churn ranges from {lr} ({lo}) to {hr} ({hi}, {n} customers): the gap shows how strongly this dimension separates leavers from stayers.

dist.title: Churners vs non-churners
dist.sub: Distribution of a numeric column for each group, drawn from stored quartiles (box = middle 50%, whiskers = 1st to 99th percentile, dashed = mean).
dist.log_disabled: Not available: this column contains zeros.
dist.so_what: The median churner has {name} of {m1} against {m0} for customers who stayed.
dist.caption: Statistics ignore empty values; see the missing-values chart for how often each column is empty.

find.title: Key findings
find.rate: {n} of {rows} customers churned ({rate}): the classes are imbalanced, which is why the model is judged on ranking (ROC-AUC) rather than accuracy.
find.missing: {col} is empty for {pct} of customers, and {n} columns are empty for more than 30% of customers: missingness is a feature, not just a nuisance.
find.regularity: Churners were active a median {c} days out of 90, against {s} days for customers who stayed: activity is the clearest behavioural signal.
find.tenure: The {level} tenure band has the highest churn rate ({rate}, {n} customers).
find.region: By region, '{level}' has the highest churn rate ({rate}, {n} customers).
find.revenue: Churn falls from {low} in the lowest revenue decile to {high} in the highest: valuable customers are also the most loyal.

eda.source: Source: aggregates of {file} exported by scripts/export_artifacts.py.

meth.title: Methodology
meth.sub: How the raw columns became model features, how the model was trained and validated, why ROC-AUC, and the limits and ethics of using it.

fe.title: Feature engineering
fe.sub: {raw} raw columns become {n} model features. The table is generated from the preprocessing config and the model's feature list.
fe.caption: All {n} model features appear exactly once. The full per-feature list is on Model & Explainability; the data dictionary is on Reports.

why.raw: Keeps the original scale; trees split on thresholds directly.
why.log: Usage and money are heavily skewed; the log compresses extreme values so a few heavy users do not dominate.
why.missing: An empty field is information: inactive lines leave usage empty, so 'not recorded' flags let the model use it.
why.region_missing: Same idea for region: a missing region is itself a strong signal.
why.region_unseen: A safe bucket for any region not seen in training.
why.onehot: Region has no natural order, so each region gets its own 0/1 column.
why.ordinal: Tenure bands are ordered, so one ordered number keeps that order.
why.freq: Hundreds of packs exist; replacing each by its popularity keeps the signal without hundreds of columns, with rare packs pooled.
why.missing_count: One summary of how much of the record is empty.
why.rev_per_recharge: Average value of each top-up: many small recharges and few large ones look different.
why.data_share: How data-heavy the customer is relative to spend.
why.unused: Constant in the training data, so it carries no signal.

train.title: Training and validation
train.sub: Read from the model's own parameters and metadata.
train.imbalance: The model was trained on the natural churn rate, without class weights or resampling. ROC-AUC measures ranking, so it is not distorted by imbalance, and leaving the data unweighted keeps the predicted probabilities close to real churn rates (see the calibration curve). Thresholds, not re-weighting, decide how many customers to flag.
train.imbalance_weighted: The model applies class weighting to counter the imbalance. Predicted probabilities may then overstate churn and should be checked against the calibration curve before being read as rates.
train.validation: A random hold-out split (seed {seed}) was kept aside. LightGBM (learning rate {lr}, {leaves} leaves per tree) added trees while the validation score improved; the best score came at iteration {best}. The deployed model has {trees} trees, about 1.1 × the best iteration, which suggests a final refit on all rows. The hold-out share is not recorded in the artifacts; the export script asks for it.
train.metric: ROC-AUC is the Zindi competition metric and it is threshold-free: it measures how well the model ranks churners above stayers, which is exactly what a retention call list needs, before anyone has agreed a cut-off. The deployed model scores {auc}. Precision, recall and costs at a chosen threshold are shown on Model Evaluation.

ethics.title: Limitations and ethics
ethics.sub: What the model cannot do, and how it should not be used.
ethics.duplicates: {n} missing-value indicators appear twice in the feature list (X_MISSING and is_missing_X). Accuracy is unaffected, but importance is split across each pair. The model was not changed.
ethics.thresholds: No business-approved risk thresholds exist. The app shows probabilities; any Low / Medium / High band is exploratory.
ethics.snapshot: The data is a single 90-day snapshot. Prices, offers and competitors change, so the model must be monitored for drift and retrained.
ethics.region: Region is missing for {pct} of customers and 'region not recorded' is the strongest signal. Regions with poorer data capture could be scored as riskier for reasons of record-keeping, not behaviour: check the fairness view before using scores regionally.
ethics.region_nopct: 'Region not recorded' is the strongest signal. Regions with poorer data capture could be scored as riskier for reasons of record-keeping, not behaviour: check the fairness view before using scores regionally.
ethics.decision_support: Predictions are decision support only. They should inform offers, never trigger penalties, disconnection or credit decisions about an individual without human review.
ethics.privacy: The app needs no names or phone numbers. Scored files and call lists contain customer IDs: handle them under Expresso's data-protection rules.
ethics.fairness_link: Open the fairness check on Model Evaluation

rar.title: Revenue at Risk
rar.sub: How much monthly revenue sits with customers likely to leave: a portfolio estimate by segment, and the expected value at risk in your scored batch.

port.title: Portfolio estimate by segment
port.sub: Customers × churn rate × median monthly revenue, per segment, building up to the total.
port.so_what: About {total} of monthly revenue sits with customers expected to churn; {seg} alone is {share} of it, so that is where retention protects the most money.
port.zero: {seg} contributes 0 to this estimate because its median monthly revenue is 0 FCFA: at least half of its customers record no revenue. Its {churn} churn rate still matters for volume, and any revenue from its paying minority is not captured by a median-based estimate.
port.caption: A median-based, order-of-magnitude estimate from segment_profiles.csv: medians are robust to outliers but understate segments with a few big spenders. Use the batch view below for customer-level values.

batch.title: Expected revenue at risk in your batch
batch.sub: Sum over customers of churn probability × REVENUE.
batch.total_help: Σ (churn probability × monthly REVENUE) over the customers in the batch.
batch.share: Share of batch revenue at risk
batch.top10: Held by the top 10% of customers
batch.top10_help: Share of the expected revenue at risk carried by the 10% of customers with the highest probability × revenue.
batch.no_rev_help: Share of the batch with REVENUE empty or 0: their churn costs no monthly revenue.
batch.by_region: Expected revenue at risk by region
batch.by_tenure: Expected revenue at risk by tenure
batch.so_what: {level} carries the most expected revenue at risk ({value}, {share} of the batch total).
batch.caption: Expected values assume the probabilities are calibrated (see Model Evaluation). Monthly revenue; multiply by your value horizon for lifetime figures.

exp.title: Experiment Designer
exp.sub: Plan an A/B test of a retention offer: how many customers each group needs, how to split the call list fairly, how long it takes, and whether the result is real.

plan.title: Sample size
plan.sub: Treatment gets the offer; control does not. Comparing their churn rates measures what the offer really changes.
plan.base: Baseline churn in the target group (%)
plan.base_help_batch: Default: the average predicted churn of the riskiest {k} customers in your batch.
plan.base_help_portfolio: Default: the portfolio churn rate. Score a batch to use your target group's predicted churn.
plan.red_help: The smallest effect worth detecting. Smaller effects need many more customers.
plan.alpha_help: Chance of declaring an effect that is not real. 0.05 is the usual choice.
plan.power_help: Chance of detecting the effect if it is real. 0.8 is the usual minimum.
plan.two_sided_help: Also detects offers that make churn worse. Recommended.
plan.weekly_help: How many treatment customers the team can contact each week.
plan.bad_effect: The expected churn after the offer must be above 0 and below the baseline.
plan.weeks: Weeks to contact the treatment group
plan.explain: To detect a drop from {base} to {target} with α = {alpha} and {power} power, put {n} customers in each group. Contacting the treatment group takes about {weeks} week(s); the control group is not contacted but is tracked the same way.

split.title: Split the priority call list
split.sub: Take the riskiest customers in your batch and assign them at random to treatment or control.
split.no_batch: Score a batch on Batch Scoring to split its priority call list into treatment and control.
split.k_help: Defaults to twice the required group size.
split.underpowered: Only {have} customers per group against the {need} needed: the test may miss a real effect. Add customers or accept a larger minimum effect.
split.caption: Random assignment with a fixed seed makes the split reproducible. Similar average predicted churn in both groups confirms the split is balanced.

res.title: Analyse results
res.sub: After the campaign, enter (or upload) how many customers in each group churned.
res.upload_help: CSV with columns group (treatment / control), customers, churned.
res.bad_file: Could not read the file. It needs columns group, customers and churned, with rows 'treatment' and 'control'.
res.example: The starting numbers are an example; replace them with your campaign's counts.
res.bad_counts: Churned cannot exceed the number of customers.
res.verdict_win: The offer worked: churn fell by {uplift} points (confidence interval {lo} to {hi} points, p = {p}). Across the treatment group that is about {saved} customers kept.
res.verdict_harm: The offer made churn worse by {uplift} points (p = {p}). Stop it and review the offer.
res.verdict_none: No reliable effect: the difference of {uplift} points could be chance (p = {p}, interval {lo} to {hi} points). Do not scale yet; test longer or with more customers.
res.so_what: Churn was {t} with the offer and {c} without; the error bars show the 95% uncertainty around each rate.

drift.title: Data Quality & Drift
drift.sub: Does the batch you scored look like the data the model learned from? Large shifts mean its predictions are less reliable.
drift.missing_detail: Drift checks compare your batch with the training distributions in reference_stats.json, exported once with:

overall.green: The batch looks like the training data: predictions can be used as usual.
overall.amber: Some columns have shifted moderately. Predictions are usable but check the flagged columns.
overall.red: Some columns look very different from the training data. Treat predictions for this batch with caution and investigate before acting.

table.title: Column by column
table.sub: PSI compares the share of customers in each training bin (deciles for numbers, categories for text, plus empty values).
table.caption: Population Stability Index: green below 0.10, amber 0.10 to 0.25, red above 0.25. Status is shown by colour, icon and text.

warn.title: Warnings
warn.red: {name} in this file looks very different from the training data (PSI {psi}); predictions may be less reliable.
warn.amber: {name} has shifted moderately from the training data (PSI {psi}); keep an eye on it.
warn.missing: {name} is empty for {new} of this batch against {ref} in training: check how the file was extracted.
warn.unseen: {name} contains values the model never saw: {values}.

chart.title: Shift by column
chart.sub: PSI per column with the 0.10 and 0.25 thresholds.
chart.dist_so_what: The biggest difference is in '{bin}': {train} of training customers against {batch} in this batch.

drift.synthetic_note: This batch is synthetic demo data, so some drift against the real training data is expected.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.sub: Raised automatically after scoring, with fixed rules.
alerts.above: {n} customers ({share}) are at or above the High threshold of {high}.
alerts.vip: {n} customers are both in the top 10% by revenue (at least {cut} per month) and in the riskiest decile: priority calls for the retention desk.
alerts.vip_none: No customer is in both the top revenue decile and the riskiest decile.
alerts.regions: Regions with unusually high average risk: {regions} (batch average {mean}).
alerts.regions_none: No region's average risk stands out (batch average {mean}).
alerts.drift_green: Data drift: the batch looks like the training data.
alerts.drift_red: Data drift: {red} column(s) shifted strongly; predictions may be less reliable.
alerts.rules: Rules: High = the 'High from' threshold above; high value = top 10% of paying customers by REVENUE; unusual region = average probability more than {factor}× the batch average with at least {min} customers.

summary.title: Executive summary
summary.sub: A one-page summary of the current state: portfolio, model, latest batch and data health, and recommended actions. Built only from the app's data and tools.

summary.by_template: Written from fixed templates filled with the app's numbers (no API key needed).
summary.pdf_sub: Generated {date} by the Churn Intelligence Hub · Team Spartans
summary.portfolio: {n} customers, overall churn {rate} (about {churners} churners). High-Value Active customers generate {rev} of revenue, while Silent / Inactive customers account for {silent} of churners.
summary.model: The LightGBM model ranks churners with a validation ROC-AUC of {auc}; its strongest signals are {d1} and {d2}.
summary.baseline: It beats the Logistic Regression baseline (ROC-AUC {lr}).
summary.revenue: About {v} of monthly revenue sits with customers expected to churn (median-based estimate).
summary.batch: {n} customers scored, average churn probability {mean}, about {exp} expected churners.
summary.no_batch: No batch has been scored in this session.
summary.drift_green: Data health: the batch looks like the training data.
summary.drift_amber: Data health: {amber} column(s) shifted moderately from the training data.
summary.drift_red: Data health: {red} column(s) shifted strongly; predictions for this batch need caution.
summary.drift_na: Data health: not checked (reference_stats.json not exported).
